notes: The whole 75-page adopted PDF, read end to end: preface, preparers, introduction to the theme, methodology and study-period justification, the five-part historic context (Native Americans and colonization, the Mexican era, establishment and expansion 1848-1860, land grants to suburbanization 1861-1880, the Gilded Age 1881-1899), the architectural characteristics and styles section, the evaluation criteria with their worked examples, and the bibliography. There is no inventory table, no appendix of survey results and no APN anywhere in the document; Appendix A is maps with no text layer of addresses. Every numbered address comes from a figure caption — the illustrated style examples in section F and the criterion-by-criterion worked examples in section G — with one from the methodology narrative and one from a bibliography image credit. Read the captions before judging a thematic statement thin.

coverage.remaining: None. The document was read in full; nothing in it is outstanding.
coverage.note: 26 numbered-address mentions across 75 pages, one per distinct address. Two further location mentions carry no street number and are not findings: the cottages on Napier Lane built c. 1875-1890, and the Pelton cottages on Tennessee Street in the Dogpatch historic district. Figure E-8/E-9 name only ‘the 600 block of Shotwell Street’; the number 648 comes from the bibliography entry crediting that photograph, so it is recorded at low confidence as an image credit rather than a claim the statement makes. Figure G-8 shows a ‘Pacific Heights 1800s Italianate home’ with no address at all. Two of the printed addresses are two-number addresses for one building (526-528 Clipper Street, 510-512 Capp Street), not rows of separate houses.
